title: Review velocity & small-refactor capture (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Spike PRs this sprint have been landing slower than expected; want to tighten review loop without sacrificing safety.
- Main pain: long diffs touching batching + kv-cache + a couple of runtime kernels. Hard to run full perf locally.
- Immediate target: get 1) faster signal for regressions (latency/cost), 2) a small safe refactor checklist for kernel callers.

Goals (what I want from reviews):
- Fast triage (<2h) for low-risk changes (docs, tests, small refactors)
- Clear gate for larger changes that affect hotpath/throughput/latency
- Actionable follow-ups captured in PR comments + tracked task created if needed

Quick heuristics (for me to remember when reviewing):
- If change touches `kv_cache.*` or `continuous_batcher.py` -> bump to slow-path review and insist on perf numbers.
- Small API-only cleanup (pure renames, docstrings) = fast-approve if CI green.
- Any change that changes default batching/window sizes = require staging perf test run.
- New dependency or native-binding -> escalate to infra + security.
- Look for hidden allocations in tight loops (lists, dicts created per-token).

Pre-merge checklist (rough order):
- ✅ Does the PR include unit tests for behavior changes? If not, ask for at least one minimal test.
- ✅ Are there benchmarks/perf runs included or a clear plan to run them? (attach numbers or GH Actions link)
- ✅ Are schema changes (proto/json) backward-compatible? If not, note migration plan.
- ✅ Does the PR update any rollouts/feature flags config (console entries)? If yes, ensure rollout plan comment.
- ✅ CI: lint + typechecks + linux integration. If flaky tests exist, call out specific flaky-test skip in PR.
- ✅ Security: new secrets/KMS/HSM contact? Tag security.

Small refactor ideas to reuse (drafted for future PRs):
1) Localize kv-cache eviction policy tests:
   - Add a tiny in-memory harness under `tests/kv_cache/` that reproduces eviction edge cases with small sequences.
   - Benefit: reviewers can run single file quickly.
2) Split continuous_batcher into: 
   - `batch_scheduler.py` (policy, timers)
   - `batch_executor.py` (io, submission)
   - Start with a thin shim to keep PR small.
   - Review risk: increases surface area — so do small steps with toggles.
3) Replace a couple of list comprehensions in `kernels/attn_fast.py` with generator-based streaming to reduce peak mem for long sequences.
   - Bench locally with seq_len=2048 to feel impact.

Observability & perf follow-ups to require on PRs that touch hotpath:
- Add perf-run gist (or GH Actions artifact) with: p50/p95 token latency, throughput (tokens/s), and memory RSS for same test input.
- If change improves latency but increases cost, require owner to add note to console cost dashboard request for aQA signoff.
- Add tracing label: `review:kv-cache` when PR touches kv cache so we can aggregate traces from staging.

Rollback and safety plan snippets (copy into PR where appropriate):
- Rollback plan: revert the PR and redeploy previous image; warm caches in staging before promotion.
- Feature flag: gate new behavior behind `FEATURE_KV_CACHE_TUNABLE` default=false for 48h rollout.
- Monitoring: add an alert for token latency > baseline * 1.25 for 30m.

Tests / perf checklist to include in PR description:
- Local unit: `pytest tests/kv_cache -k eviction` ran: yes/no + stdout attached.
- Microbench: `bench/run_local.sh --seq 2048 --workers 2` + attach csv.
- Integration: checked against staging config with minimal traffic.

Example tiny snippet to call out in reviews (watch for hidden allocs):
- Bad:
    for i in range(n):
        tmp = [x for x in tokens]  # copies slice each call
        process(tmp)
- Better:
    it = iter(tokens)
    process(it)

Common review comments I use (templates):
- "Can you add a microbench and include the run logs? We need a clear perf signal for the deployment decision."
- "This looks like a behavior change for existing clients; please document the migration (example inputs/outputs)."
- "Suggest extracting a small helper so we can unit-test this path in isolation — avoids flakey integration test debugging."

Open TODOs (my action list after reviewing a PR):
- [ ] Run bench with 2x seq_len and compare mem/latency for before/after.
- [ ] Add a staging smoke test that hits a small batcher loop (5 concurrent requests).
- [ ] If we can't reproduce perf regression locally, request a canary run and short window (2h) in staging.

Notes to self / post-review follow-ups:
- When approving microrefactor, leave a comment: "Acked small refactor — landing once CI + bench artifacts posted." Keeps ownership explicit.
- If change touches a kernel but is small, ping kernel owner for optional eyeball.
- For big batching changes, schedule a 20-min sync instead of back-and-forth comments. Saves time.

Random brainstorming (parking lot):
- Could we make a GH action that automatically runs a minimal perf harness for PRs that touch files under `/kernels` or `/batching`? If yes, we get an automated baseline on every PR.
- Thoughts: run with tiny inputs in GH (fast) but also trigger an optional longer run on-demand that posts artifacts to PR when requested.

Last-minute checklist before approving (mental):
- No surprising allocations?
- Tests cover behavior?
- Perf signal exists or plan to get one?
- Rollout/fallback described?

-- end --
(If I forget, search GH for `PR-812` and pick up the context; linked artifacts above.)
